[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/debugging/]
## Debugging

The framework includes debug logs that can be useful if you encounter an error that is not sufficiently descriptive. For instance, you might face a WebSocket server error due to an incorrect `Player.exe` path. Enabling debug logs can provide insights such as “Spawning player executable with path: …”, helping you identify the issue.

To enable debug logs, execute the `gameface-e2e` command as follows:

**Bash terminal:**

```shell
DEBUG=oclif:gameface-e2e* npx gameface-e2e
```

On Windows, you can use the following command:

**PowerShell:**

```shell
$env:DEBUG = "oclif:gameface-e2e*"; npx gameface-e2e
```

**Command Prompt:**

```shell
cmd /C "set DEBUG=oclif:gameface-e2e* && npx gameface-e2e"
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/gf-over-domelement/]
## GF object and DOMElement

Gameface e2e testing framework provides two main ways to interact with UI elements: the `gf` object and the `DOMElement` object. Each serves a different purpose and is suited for different scenarios. Understanding when to use each can help you write more efficient and effective tests.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/gf-over-domelement/#gf-object]
## GF object and DOMElement: gf object

The `gf` object is a global utility that provides methods to interact with the UI elements. It is typically used for quick, single actions, such as retrieving the text of an element without further interaction.

#### Example

Here is an example of using the `gf` object to get the text of an element:

```js
describe('Test script', function () {
    it('Test 1', async () => {
        const text = await gf.text('.my-element');
        assert.equal(text, 'Hello, World!');
    });
});
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/gf-over-domelement/#domelement-object]
## GF object and DOMElement: DOMElement object

The `DOMElement` object, on the other hand, represents a specific DOM element and is ideal for scenarios where multiple interactions with the same element are required. For instance, you might retrieve an element, check its text, and then perform a click action.

#### Example

Here is an example of using the `DOMElement` object to perform multiple actions on the same element:

```js
describe('Test script', function () {
    it('Test 1', async () => {
        const element = await gf.get('.my-element');
        const text = await element.text();
        assert.equal(text, 'Hello, World!');
        await element.click();
    });
});
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/gf-over-domelement/#summary]
## GF object and DOMElement: Summary

Use the `gf` object for simplicity when only one interaction is needed, and opt for the `DOMElement` object when you need to perform multiple operations on the same element.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/multiple-processes/]
## Running multiple test processes in parallel

The framework allows running multiple test processes simultaneously. Each test process spawns a separate Gameface Player instance on a different port if the current one is occupied.

This feature enables you to execute multiple test processes independently and in parallel, which can significantly reduce the overall test execution time.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/multiple-processes/#example]
## Running multiple test processes in parallel: Example

In this example, we will use the `concurrently` npm module to run two test processes in parallel. Alternatively, you can create your own script to manage multiple processes and handle their exit codes.

First, install the `concurrently` module:

```shell
npm install --save-dev concurrently
```

Next, add the following script to the `scripts` section of your project’s `package.json`:

```json
"scripts": {
    ...
    "test": "concurrently --kill-others-on-fail \"gameface-e2e --tests=./tests/view1/**/*.spec.js --gamefacePath=../Gameface/Player/Player.exe\" \"gameface-e2e --tests=./tests/view2/**/*.spec.js --gamefacePath=../Gameface/Player/Player.exe\""
    ...
}
```

You can also use separate configuration files to run different test processes:

```json
"scripts": {
    ...
    "test": "concurrently --kill-others-on-fail \"gameface-e2e --config=./tests/view1.config.js\" \"gameface-e2e --config=./tests/view2.config.js\""
    ...
}
```

In each configuration file, specify the `tests` and `gamefacePath` properties.

Now, running `npm run test` will start two `Player` processes, each executing tests for a specific view in parallel.

**Tip:** If you are using bash terminal and want to keep your `package.json` organized, you can follow these steps:

1. Create a `run-e2e.sh` script:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
concurrently --kill-others-on-fail \
    "gameface-e2e --config=./tests/view1.config.js" \
    "gameface-e2e --config=./tests/view2.config.js"
```

2. Update the `scripts` section in your `package.json`:

```json
"scripts": {
    "test": "bash ./run-e2e.sh"
}
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/waiting-for-element/]
## Waiting for the right element state

Validating changes in an element’s state within the UI can sometimes lead to unreliable test results. For instance, clicking a button that modifies an element’s size might cause the test to fail if the size change hasn’t occurred by the time the validation runs. This happens because UI updates are often asynchronous and may take time to reflect.

Methods prone to such issues include:

- `element.getSize`
- `element.getPositionOnScreen`
- `element.isVisible`
- `element.isVisibleInScrollableArea`
- `element.isHidden`
- `element.isScrollable`
- `gf.isHidden`
- `gf.isVisible`

Other methods that depend on the UI’s state post-interaction may also exhibit similar problems. The following guide outlines an effective approach to address these challenges.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/waiting-for-element/#use-gfretryiffails]
## Waiting for the right element state: Use gf.retryIfFails

To handle asynchronous UI updates, leverage the `gf.retryIfFails` method. This utility retries the provided function until it succeeds or times out, ensuring the element’s state has changed before proceeding with validation.

#### Example

Below is an example demonstrating how to use `gf.retryIfFails` to wait for an element’s size to update after a click. The test clicks an element to trigger a size change and then validates the updated size:

```js
describe('Test script', function () {
    it('Test 1', async () => {
        const element = await gf.get('.my-element');
        await element.click(); // Trigger a size change
        await gf.retryIfFails(async () => {
            const size = await element.getSize();
            assert(size.width > 100, 'Element width should be greater than 100');
        });
    });
});
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/waiting-for-element/#gfretryiffails-parameters]
## Waiting for the right element state: gf.retryIfFails Parameters

The `gf.retryIfFails` method accepts the following parameters:

- **`action`**: The function to execute, which should return a promise. If the promise resolves successfully, the retry stops; if it rejects, the retry continues until the timeout is reached.
- **`retryCount`** (optional): The number of times to retry the action. Defaults to 10. Each retry waits for 100 milliseconds before executing the action again.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/waiting-for-element/#enhanced-assert-methods]
## Waiting for the right element state: Enhanced assert methods 1.1.0

Version `1.1.0` introduced additional methods to the `DOMElement` object for easier validation of element states. These methods internally retry the validation, eliminating the need to use `gf.retryIfFails` directly in your tests.

For example:

```js
describe('Test script', function () {
    it('Test 1', async () => {
        const element = await gf.get('.my-element');
        // Clicking the button makes the element visible
        await gf.click('.btn');
        // This approach may result in flaky tests if the element isn't immediately visible after the click
        assert.equal(await element.isVisible(), true, 'Element should be visible');
        // This method retries the visibility check until it passes or times out. If the element remains invisible after the timeout, an error is thrown with a descriptive message.
        assert(await element.waitForVisibility(true));
    });
});
```

For more details on the new assert methods, refer to the DOMElement Assert methods documentation.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/concepts/writing-tests/]
## Writing tests

To write tests for your UI in Gameface, you can use the `gf` object provided by the testing framework. The `gf` object provides various methods to interact with the UI, such as clicking elements, getting the element properties, etc.

Here is a simple example of a test file:

```js
describe("Test my UI", () => {
    it("Should display the correct text", async () => {
        const element = await gf.get('.my-element');
        const text = await element.text();
        assert.equal(text, 'Hello, World!');
    });

    it("Should update the text when clicked", async () => {
        const btn = await gf.get('.my-button');
        await btn.click();
        const element = await gf.get('.my-element');
        const text = await element.text();
        assert.equal(text, 'Hello, Gameface!');
    });
});
```

To see more examples of how to write tests, check the `examples` folder in the gameface-e2e npm package. The examples include various test cases demonstrating how to use the `gf` object and its methods.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/getting-started/]
## Overview

Gameface E2E an end-to-end (E2E) JavaScript testing framework for Gameface, capable of running tests on UIs created with Gameface. It utilizes the DevTools protocol to execute commands on Gameface and provides various commands to interact with the UI.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/getting-started/installation/]
## Installation

To install the testing framework in your project, run the following command:

```shell
npm install gameface-e2e --save-dev
```

Alternatively, you can install it globally:

```shell
npm install gameface-e2e -g
```

**We recommend using Node.js version 20 or higher.**

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/getting-started/usage/]
## Usage

To run tests with the `gameface-e2e` framework, you need the following:

1. `Player.exe` located at `${GamefacePackage}/Player/Player.exe`.
2. `.spec` files to be executed. The framework uses [`mocha`](https://mochajs.org/), so your `.spec` files should follow the `describe`-`it` pattern.
3. (Optional) A config file for running the tests.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/getting-started/usage/#running-tests-without-a-config-file]
## Usage: Running tests without a config file

To run your tests without a config file, use the following command:

```shell
npx gameface-e2e --gamefacePath=${PATH_TO_PLAYER_EXE} --tests=${PATH_TO_SPEC_FILES}
```

If you have installed the framework globally, you can use:

```shell
gameface-e2e --gamefacePath=${PATH_TO_PLAYER_EXE} --tests=${PATH_TO_SPEC_FILES}
```

- `PATH_TO_PLAYER_EXE`: The path to your `Player.exe`, either relative to the command execution location or as an absolute path.
- `PATH_TO_SPEC_FILES`: The path to your spec files, either relative to the command execution location or as an absolute path. You can use patterns like `tests/**/*.spec.js` to match all `.spec` files in the `tests` folder.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/e2e/getting-started/usage/#running-tests-with-a-config-file]
## Usage: Running tests with a config file

To avoid specifying the `gamefacePath` and `tests` paths each time you run your tests, you can create a config file that the framework will use to retrieve both flags.

There are two ways to do this:

1. Create a `gameface-e2e-config.js` file in the directory where you plan to run the `gameface-e2e` command, such as your project root.
2. Create a config JavaScript file with any name and place it anywhere.

Inside this file, you can specify various config properties for the testing library. Here is an example where we specify the path to the Player.exe and tests:

```js
module.exports = {
    tests: "examples/**/*.spec.js",
    gamefacePath: "C:/Gameface/Player/Player.exe"
}
```

When you configure both properties inside your config file, there are two ways to execute the `gameface-e2e` command without specifying the required flags:

1. **Without specifying the config file path.** Create a file named `gameface-e2e-config.js` in the directory where you will execute the command:
   ```shell
   npx gameface-e2e
   ```
2. **By specifying the config file path.** Pass the path to your config file, which must be relative to the location where the command will be executed:
   ```shell
   npx gameface-e2e --config=./tests/my-config.js
   ```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/changelog/#131]
## Changelog: 1.3.1 Latest

Fix Fixed declarations inside SCSS suffix selectors (`&-option`, `&__item`, `&--active`) not being linted in `.scss` files.

Previously the CSS parser could not read these selectors, so the whole enclosing block—including any nested `&:hover` rules and following sibling blocks—was skipped and no Gameface errors were reported for it:

```scss
.dropdown {
    display: grid; // reported

    &-option {
        display: grid; // was not reported, now reported

        &:hover {
            display: grid; // was not reported, now reported
        }
    }
}
```

This works automatically with the `flat/recommended` preset—no configuration changes are needed.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/changelog/#130]
## Changelog: 1.3.0

Feature Added a config option to set specific Gameface target version.

This can be done by adding the `version` field under the `gameface` settings in your ESLint configuration, as shown below:

```js
import gameface from "eslint-plugin-gameface";

export default [
  {
    ignores: ["**/node_modules/**"],
  },
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    settings: {
      gameface: {
        version: "3.1.2.1",
      }
    },
    files: ["examples/**/*"],
    rules: {
      "css/use-baseline": "off",
    },
  },
];
```

For more information about the supported version check the following section in the documentation: Enabling linter for a specific Gameface version.

[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/changelog/#100]
## Changelog: 1.0.0

Feature First release of ESLint support for Gameface projects: HTML, CSS, SCSS, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX.

Feature Recommended flat config preset to catch unsupported CSS, HTML, data binding, SVG, and JS API usage before runtime.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/]
## Overview

Use **eslint-plugin-gameface** in your projects to catch unsupported or risky Gameface patterns **during development**, instead of at runtime.

The plugin checks the same kinds of problems you would hit in Gameface for:

- **CSS and SCSS** — properties, functions, selectors, and documented limits (for example `var()` inside `@keyframes`)
- **HTML** — unsupported or partial elements, inline and embedded styles, data binding attributes
- **JSX / TSX** — inline styles, data binding, and SVG markup in components
- **Vue SFC** (`.vue`) — template, script, and `<style>` blocks with the same checks as HTML/JSX/CSS
- **Svelte SFC** (`.svelte`) — markup, script, and `<style>` blocks with the same checks as HTML/JSX/CSS
- **JavaScript / TypeScript** — globals and APIs that Gameface does not support or only partially supports

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#recommended-setup]
## Configuration: Recommended setup

Add this to `eslint.config.js` in your project root:

```js
import gameface from "eslint-plugin-gameface";

export default [
  { ignores: ["**/node_modules/**", "dist/**"] },
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
];
```

That preset turns on Gameface checks for:

Files | Examples of what is checked
`*.html` | Unsupported tags, `data-bind-*`, `<style>` and `style=""`
`*.css`, `*.scss` | Unsupported properties, selectors, functions
`*.js`, `*.jsx` | Unsupported globals; JSX adds data binding and inline styles
`*.ts`, `*.tsx` | Same as JS/JSX
`*.vue` | Template tags, `data-bind-*`, `:style`, SVG; `<script>` JS/TS APIs; `<style>` CSS
`*.svelte` | Markup tags, `data-bind-*`, `style`, SVG; `<script>` JS/TS APIs; `<style>` CSS

The preset bundles `vue-eslint-parser` and `eslint-plugin-vue` for `.vue` files, and `svelte-eslint-parser` and `eslint-plugin-svelte` for `.svelte` files—you do not add separate Vue or Svelte ESLint configs.

Adjust `ignores` to match your build output folders.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#data-binding-models]
## Configuration: Data binding models

If you use Gameface model JSON files, point ESLint at the folder so bindings can be validated against real model fields:

```js
export default [
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    settings: {
      gameface: {
        modelsDir: "Gameface-models",
      },
    },
  },
];
```

`modelsDir` is resolved from the directory where you run ESLint (usually the project root). Change it if your models live elsewhere.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#custom-data-bind-attributes]
## Configuration: Custom data-bind attributes

If your project uses extra `data-bind-*` attribute names, allow them so spelling rules do not report false positives:

```json
settings: {
  gameface: {
    customDataBindAttributes: ["data-bind-my-feature"],
  },
},
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#gf-versions]
## Configuration: Enabling linter for a specific Gameface version

By default, rules use the **latest** support data shipped with the plugin. If your team targets an older Gameface release, you can specify it in the ESLint configuration:

```json
settings: {
  gameface: {
    version: "3.1.2.1",
  },
},
```

Supported values: `"latest"` (default, currently `3.1.4.1`), or one of the bundled versions below. Any other string still works — it resolves to the nearest bundled version with a console warning instead of failing.

- `3.1.4.1` Latest
- `3.1.3.3`
- `3.1.2.1`

Only set this when your project actually depends on that version’s support tables. Most teams can leave the default.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#change-rule-severity-or-turn-rules-off]
## Configuration: Change rule severity or turn rules off

Add a `rules` block after the preset. Use `"off"`, `"warn"`, or `"error"`; some rules also accept options:

```js
export default [
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    rules: {
      "gameface/html-partial-features": "off",
      "gameface/js-partial-member-access": "warn",
      "gameface/html-parsed-no-impl": [
        "error",
        { scope: "all", ignoreTags: ["meta", "link"] },
      ],
    },
  },
];
```

See Configure rules and the full rule list with descriptions and defaults.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/configuration/#ide-still-shows-other-css-warnings]
## Configuration: IDE still shows other CSS warnings?

`gameface/css-no-unsupported-properties` only reports properties Gameface does not support. Your editor may still underline `coh-*` or other vendor properties as “unknown” from **VS Code CSS validation**, not from this plugin.

To reduce noise:

- Add [VS Code `css.customData`](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/css#_css-specific-settings) for Gameface specific properties, or
- Relax editor CSS lint settings for Gameface stylesheets.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/installation/]
## Installation

Install **ESLint** and **eslint-plugin-gameface**. The plugin ships with the HTML, CSS, Vue, and Svelte SFC tooling its preset uses (`@html-eslint/eslint-plugin`, `@eslint/css`, `vue-eslint-parser`, `eslint-plugin-vue`, `svelte-eslint-parser`, `eslint-plugin-svelte`, and the TypeScript parser for `.ts` / `.tsx` / `<script lang="ts">`) - you do not install those separately.

```shell
npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-plugin-gameface
```

**Requirements:**

- ESLint **9.15+** with [flat config](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/configuration-files).
- Use Node.js `>=18.18.0` version. **We recomend to use latest versions of Node.js.**

After you configure the plugin, you can verify its work from the terminal:

```shell
npx eslint .
```

You should see `gameface/...` messages on HTML, CSS, JSX, Vue, or Svelte files that use unsupported Gameface features.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/installation/#vs-code-edit-time-hints]
## Installation: VS Code (edit-time hints) (1/2)

Terminal ESLint does not add squiggles in the editor by itself. For **inline diagnostics while you type**, install the [ESLint extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=dbaeumer.vscode-eslint) (`dbaeumer.vscode-eslint`).

1. Install the extension from the VS Code Marketplace.
2. Ensure your project has `eslint.config.js` with the recommended preset.
3. Open an HTML, CSS, JSX, Vue, or Svelte file—the Problems panel and editor underlines should show `gameface/` issues.

#### Validate HTML, CSS, Vue, Svelte, and other file types

By default, the ESLint extension mainly lints JavaScript and TypeScript. To run ESLint (and Gameface rules) **while you edit** `.html`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, and JSX/TSX files, add `eslint.validate` to your workspace or user settings.

Create or edit `.vscode/settings.json` in your project:

```json
{
  "eslint.validate": [
    "javascript", // Enables Javascript files validation (.js)
    "javascriptreact", // Enables Javascript React files validation (.jsx)
    "typescript", // Enables Typescript files validation (.ts)
    "typescriptreact", // Enables Typescript React files validation (.tsx)
    "css", // Enables CSS files validation (.css)
    "html", // Enables HTML files validation (.html)
    "scss", // Enables SCSS files validation (.scss)
    "vue", // Enables Vue files validation (.vue)
    "svelte" // Enables Svelte files validation (.svelte)
  ]
}
```

or add the same to your global VS Code settings (Command Palette → Preferences: Open Settings (JSON)).

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/getting-started/installation/#vs-code-edit-time-hints]
## Installation: VS Code (edit-time hints) (2/2)

After that, reload the window or run **ESLint: Restart ESLint Server** command (`Ctrl + Shift + P`) to apply the new changes.

If nothing appears, check that ESLint is enabled for the workspace (Command Palette → **ESLint: Show Output Channel**) and that the file type is not excluded in VS Code or ESLint `ignores`.

Other editors (WebStorm, Neovim, etc.) have their own ESLint integrations; the same `eslint.config.js` applies.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/data-binding/]
## Data binding

Gameface data binding attributes are easy to mistype. The plugin flags common mistakes in **HTML** and **JSX** before you load the page in the engine.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/data-binding/#typical-issues-caught]
## Data binding: Typical issues caught

Problem | Example | Notes
Unknown attribute name | `data-bind-typo="{{Model.name}}"`
Missing `{{ }}` | `data-bind-value="Model.name"`
Broken model path | `data-bind-value="{{Model.}}"` | Configure the path to your mock models folder first so the linter is able to validate their usage in the `data-bind-*` attributes!
Invalid `bind-for` | Semicolon or wrong iterator syntax
Wrong class toggle format | Missing `class:{{condition}}` pattern
Unknown model field | Path does not exist in your model JSON

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/data-binding/#models]
## Data binding: Point ESLint at your models

Models validation compares bindings to JSON files in your models folder:

```js
settings: {
  gameface: {
    modelsDir: "Gameface-models",
  },
},
```

**Note:** The folder path should be relative to your eslint config.

**Note:** The default folder configured in the flat config is `Gameface-models`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/data-binding/#custom-bind-attributes]
## Data binding: Custom bind attributes

Projects sometimes add proprietary `data-bind-*` names. Register them so they are not reported as spelling errors:

```js
settings: {
  gameface: {
    customDataBindAttributes: ["data-bind-custom-widget"],
  },
},
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/data-binding/#html-and-jsx-use-the-same-rules]
## Data binding: HTML and JSX use the same rules

HTML files use `gameface/html-databind-*` rules. React/Solid-style components use the matching `gameface/jsx-databind-*` rules on the opening tag.

If you previously used [**HTMLLint**](https://docs.coherent-labs.com/cpp-gameface/content_development/htmllint/) plugin for the same checks, you can move those workflows to ESLint with the preset above and the same `modelsDir` / `customDataBindAttributes` settings you used in `.cohtmllintrc`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/javascript/]
## JavaScript and TypeScript

Scripts can call APIs that Gameface does not provide/support. The plugin flags **obvious** unsupported usage in `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, and `.tsx` files.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/javascript/#what-you-will-see]
## JavaScript and TypeScript: What you will see

- **Errors** for globals Gameface does not support (for example some browser-only APIs used as bare identifiers)
- **Warnings** for partial APIs—`Something.member` where `member` is known to be missing on that type in Gameface

These are **static** checks. They help during development but do not replace testing in the actual Gameface runtime.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/javascript/#examples-of-patterns-that-may-not-be-reported]
## JavaScript and TypeScript: Examples of patterns that may not be reported

- `obj.chrome` or other property access through a variable
- `globalThis['Chrome']` with a computed name
- Code paths only reachable at runtime

**Note:** TypeScript files are linted without full type information from your `tsconfig`, so the plugin does not use the TypeScript compiler to prove a global exists.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/javascript/#if-a-warning-is-wrong-for-your-build]
## JavaScript and TypeScript: If a warning is wrong for your build

Some projects polyfill or inject globals at runtime. You can lower severity or disable the rule for that file pattern:

```js
{
  files: ["src/legacy/**/*.js"],
  rules: {
    "gameface/js-no-unsupported-globals": "off",
  },
},
```

See Rules reference for rule ids.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/]
## Rules reference

Every Gameface rule uses the `gameface/` prefix. Defaults below match the `flat/recommended` preset.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#configure-rules-in-eslintconfigjs]
## Rules reference: Configure rules in eslint.config.js

Add a config object **after** you spread the preset so your overrides win.

#### Turn a rule off

```js
export default [
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    rules: {
      "gameface/html-partial-features": "off",
    },
  },
];
```

#### Severity only: error or warn

```js
rules: {
  "gameface/css-partial-selectors": "warn",
  "gameface/js-partial-member-access": "error",
},
```

#### Severity plus options

Some rules accept a second argument (options object):

```js
rules: {
  "gameface/html-parsed-no-impl": [
    "error",
    {
      scope: "all",
      ignoreTags: ["meta", "link", "noscript"],
    },
  ],
  "gameface/html-partial-features": [
    "warn",
    { mode: "attribute-checks", warnAllowlist: false },
  ],
},
```

#### Only for certain files

```js
export default [
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    files: ["legacy/**/*.html"],
    rules: {
      "gameface/html-parsed-no-impl": "off",
    },
  },
];
```

Severity | Meaning
`"error"` | Fails ESLint (and usually CI)
`"warn"` | Shows a warning; does not fail unless you use `--max-warnings 0`
`"off"` | Rule is disabled

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (1/13)

#### CSS and SCSS files (.css, .scss)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/css-no-unsupported-properties` | error | A property Gameface does not support (for example from your unsupported CSS list).
`gameface/css-partial-property-values` | error | A **value** on a property that is only partly supported (often a keyword Gameface rejects).
`gameface/css-no-unsupported-functions` | error | A CSS function Gameface marks as missing (for example `clamp()`, `min()`).
`gameface/css-no-unsupported-selectors` | error | A selector or pseudo-class Gameface does not support.
`gameface/css-partial-selectors` | warn | A selector/pseudo that works in browsers but is only partially supported in Gameface.
`gameface/css-no-var-in-keyframes` | error | `var()` used inside `@keyframes` (documented Gameface limit).
`gameface/css-no-calc-in-keyframes` | error | `calc()` used inside `@keyframes`.
`gameface/css-var-no-fallback` | error | `var(--name, fallback)` — second argument (fallback) is not allowed.
`gameface/css-calc-no-mixed-percent-units` | error | `calc()` mixes `%` with px/rem/etc. (for example `calc(50% - 20px)`).
`gameface/css-svg-keyframes-sizing-units` | error | In SVG-related `@keyframes`, `width` / `height` / `font-size` need units (not bare numbers).
`gameface/css-svg-keyframes-path-arc-animation` | warn | `@keyframes` animates SVG path `d` with elliptical arc commands.
`gameface/css-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | `stroke-dasharray` / `stroke-dashoffset` on a non-`<path>` SVG selector.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (2/13)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/css-svg-keyframes-stroke-dash-path-only` | warn | `@keyframes` animates stroke dash properties (only effective on `<path>` in Gameface).

#### HTML — tags and attributes (.html)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/html-parsed-no-impl` | error | An HTML tag Gameface parses but does not implement. Default **curated** scope focuses on tags like `<select>`, table model, `<iframe>`; use option `scope: "all"` for every parsed-no-impl tag.
`gameface/html-partial-features` | warn | A tag/attribute combination that is only partly supported (default: attribute-based checks).\ **Options**: `mode`, `warnAllowlist`.

#### HTML — CSS in <style> or style=""

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (3/13)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/html-embedded-css-no-unsupported-properties` | error | Unsupported property inside a `<style>` block.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-partial-property-values` | error | Unsupported keyword/value on a partial property in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-no-unsupported-functions` | error | Unsupported CSS function in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-no-unsupported-selectors` | error | Unsupported selector/pseudo in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-partial-selectors` | warn | Partially supported selector in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-no-var-in-keyframes` | error | `var()` in `@keyframes` in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-no-calc-in-keyframes` | error | `calc()` in `@keyframes` in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-var-no-fallback` | error | `var()` with fallback in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-calc-no-mixed-percent-units` | error | Mixed `%` in `calc()` in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-svg-keyframes-sizing-units` | error | SVG keyframe sizing units in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-svg-keyframes-path-arc-animation` | warn | SVG path arc animation in `<style>` keyframes.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | Stroke dash on non-path in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-embedded-css-svg-keyframes-stroke-dash-path-only` | warn | Stroke dash keyframes in `<style>`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-no-unsupported-properties` | error | Unsupported property in `style="..."`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (4/13)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/html-inline-css-partial-property-values` | error | Partial property value in `style="..."`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-no-unsupported-functions` | error | Unsupported function in `style="..."`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-no-var-in-keyframes` | error | `var()` in keyframes inside inline `style` (when parsed as CSS).
`gameface/html-inline-css-no-calc-in-keyframes` | error | `calc()` in keyframes inside inline `style`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-var-no-fallback` | error | `var()` fallback in inline `style`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-calc-no-mixed-percent-units` | error | Mixed `%` in `calc()` in inline `style`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-svg-keyframes-sizing-units` | error | SVG keyframe sizing in inline `style`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-svg-keyframes-path-arc-animation` | warn | SVG path arc keyframes in inline `style`.
`gameface/html-inline-css-svg-keyframes-stroke-dash-path-only` | warn | Stroke dash keyframes in inline `style`.

#### Data binding — HTML and JSX

[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (12/13)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/html-databind-spelling` | error | Unknown or misspelled `data-bind-*` attribute name.
`gameface/html-databind-curly-brackets` | error | Binding value missing `{{` / `}}`.
`gameface/html-databind-property-accessors` | error | Broken model path (for example `{{Model.}}`, split braces).

`gameface/html-databind-class-toggle` | error | Invalid `data-bind-class-toggle` segment (`class:{{condition}}`).

`gameface/jsx-databind-model-properties` | warn | Same as HTML, on JSX.

#### JavaScript and TypeScript

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/js-no-unsupported-globals` | error | Use of a global object/API Gameface does not provide.
`gameface/js-partial-member-access` | warn | Access to `Something.member` where `member` is known to be missing on that type in Gameface.

#### SVG in HTML and JSX

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/rules-reference/#rules]
## Rules reference: Rules (13/13)

Rule id | Default | What it reports
`gameface/html-svg-no-unsupported-elements` | error | SVG tag or SMIL element not supported inside HTML `<svg>`.
`gameface/jsx-svg-no-unsupported-elements` | error | Same, inside JSX `<svg>`.
`gameface/html-svg-mask-clip-path-conflict` | warn | Both `mask` and `clip-path` use `url(#…)` on the same element.
`gameface/jsx-svg-mask-clip-path-conflict` | warn | Same, in JSX.
`gameface/html-svg-tspan-ignored` | off | Optional: `<tspan>` styling is merged into parent `<text>` (enable with `"warn"` if you want the hint).
`gameface/html-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | `stroke-dasharray` / `stroke-dashoffset` on a shape other than `<path>`.
`gameface/jsx-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | Same, in JSX (attributes or inline style).
`gameface/vue-svg-no-unsupported-elements` | error | Same, inside Vue `<template>` `<svg>`.
`gameface/vue-svg-mask-clip-path-conflict` | warn | Same, in Vue templates.
`gameface/vue-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | Same, in Vue templates.
`gameface/svelte-svg-no-unsupported-elements` | error | Same, inside Svelte markup `<svg>`.
`gameface/svelte-svg-mask-clip-path-conflict` | warn | Same, in Svelte markup.
`gameface/svelte-svg-stroke-dash-non-path` | error | Same, in Svelte markup.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/]
## Styles and HTML markup

Most Gameface related issues in day-to-day work show up as **CSS** or **HTML** problems. The plugin surfaces them as ESLint messages with the `gameface/` prefix.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#css-files]
## Styles and HTML markup: CSS files

In `.css` and `.scss` you may see errors for:

- **Unsupported properties** — for example properties Gameface’s support tables list as missing
- **Partial properties** — the property exists but a specific value (often a keyword) is not supported
- **Unsupported functions** — such as `clamp()`, `min()`, or `max()` where Gameface marks them missing
- **Selectors** — pseudos Gameface does not implement, or only partially supports
- **Keyframes and variables** — patterns documented as unsupported, like `var()` inside `@keyframes` or `calc(50% - 20px)` mixing percent and pixels

Fix the stylesheet or adjust the rule if your team accepts the risk and wants to silence that diagnostic.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#html-markup]
## Styles and HTML markup: HTML markup

In `.html` you may see:

- **Unsupported elements** — tags Gameface parses but does not implement (the default preset focuses on a curated set such as `<select>`, table layout tags, `<iframe>`, rather than every heading or paragraph)
- **Partial elements** — warnings when you use an attribute Gameface does not support on that tag
- The same **CSS checks** inside `<style>` blocks and on `style="..."` attributes

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#jsx-components]
## Styles and HTML markup: JSX components

For components, put styles in `.css` files when possible.

If you use inline styles, the linter checks both common JSX forms:

- **Object** `style={{ alignContent: 'space-between' }}` — unsupported **property names** and bad **values** on keys (for example a typo like `alingContent`)
- **String** `style="display: flex; gap: clamp(1rem, 2rem, 3rem)"` — the full CSS string, including unsupported **functions** and keyframes rules

Some checks (functions, `var()` in keyframes, mixed `%` in `calc()`) apply only to **string** styles, not object literals. See Rules reference — JSX `style` props.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#vue-components]
## Styles and HTML markup: Vue components

For `.vue` single-file components, checks mirror JSX and HTML:

- **`:style` object** — property names and partial values on keys (for example `:style="{ alignContent: 'stretch' }"`)
- **`:style` / `style` string** — full CSS text, including functions and keyframe limits
- **`data-bind-*`** — plain or bound (`:data-bind-value="..."`) attributes in the template
- **`<style>` blocks** — the same rules as `.css` files (`vue-sfc-css-*`)

See Vue SFC and Rules reference — Vue `:style`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#svelte-components]
## Styles and HTML markup: Svelte components

For `.svelte` single-file components, checks mirror JSX and HTML:

- **`style={object}`** — property names and partial values on keys (when an object literal is used)
- **`style="..."` / `style={\`…\`}\`** — full CSS text, including functions and keyframe limits
- **`data-bind-*`** — plain attributes or expressions in markup (`data-bind-value="{Model.score}"`)
- **`<style>` blocks** — the same rules as `.css` files (`svelte-sfc-css-*`)

See Svelte SFC and Rules reference — Svelte `style`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/styles-and-markup/#partial-support-warnings]
## Styles and HTML markup: Partial support warnings

Some rules default to **warn** instead of **error** (for example partial selectors or partial JS APIs). Treat them as “works in browser, may fail or behave differently in Gameface” and fix or suppress per team policy.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/]
## Svelte SFC

Svelte **single-file components** (`.svelte`) are linted by the recommended preset. The plugin parses the SFC with `svelte-eslint-parser` and runs Gameface checks on each block.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/#what-is-checked-per-block]
## Svelte SFC: What is checked per block

Block | Rules (prefix) | Notes
Markup | `svelte-*`, `svelte-inline-css-*`, `svelte-databind-*`, `svelte-svg-*` | Same coverage as HTML/JSX for tags, `style`, `data-bind-*`, and inline SVG
`<script>` / `<script lang="ts">` | `js-*` | Unsupported globals and partial API access (JS or TS via nested parser)
`<style>` / `<style lang="scss">` | `svelte-sfc-css-*` | Same CSS checks as `.css` files and HTML `<style>` blocks

You do **not** need to install `svelte-eslint-parser` or `eslint-plugin-svelte` separately—they are dependencies of **eslint-plugin-gameface**. The preset registers them for `**/*.svelte` files.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/#style--expression-vs-string]
## Svelte SFC: style — expression vs string

The linter handles common Svelte forms:

- **String** — `style="display: flex"` or `style={`color: red;`}` (template literal). Full CSS text is parsed, including unsupported **functions**, keyframe limits, and SVG keyframe rules.
- **Expression** — `style={expr}` where `expr` is a string literal, template literal, or object literal (when used). Property names and partial **values** on object keys are checked (`svelte-inline-css-*`).

Some restrictions (for example `var()` inside `@keyframes` in a style string) apply only to **string** styles, not object literals—same as JSX. See Rules reference — Svelte `style`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/#data-bind--in-markup]
## Svelte SFC: data-bind-* in markup

Gameface data binding works with plain attributes and Svelte expressions:

```svelte
<div data-bind-value="{Model.score}"></div>
<div data-bind-value={`{Model.score}`}></div>
```

Svelte uses `{expression}` in attribute values. All six `svelte-databind-*` rules mirror the HTML and JSX counterparts. See Data binding.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/#example-eslintconfigjs]
## Svelte SFC: Example eslint.config.js

```js
import gameface from "eslint-plugin-gameface";

export default [
  { ignores: ["**/node_modules/**", "dist/**"] },
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    settings: {
      gameface: {
        modelsDir: "Gameface-models",
      },
    },
  },
];
```

No extra `.svelte` block is required—the preset includes parser, processor (for `eslint-disable` comment directives), and all `svelte-*` / `svelte-sfc-css-*` rules.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svelte/#vs-code]
## Svelte SFC: VS Code

Add `"svelte"` to `eslint.validate` so the ESLint extension lints `.svelte` files while you edit. See Installation.

For every rule id and default severity, see Rules reference.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svg/]
## SVG in UI

SVG inside your **HTML, JSX/TSX, Vue templates, or Svelte markup** is checked against Gameface’s SVG support. Standalone `.svg` files in `assets/` are not linted by this plugin—embed or reference SVG in components and pages you lint.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svg/#common-problems]
## SVG in UI: Common problems

Issue | What to do
Unsupported SVG tag or SMIL element | Replace with a supported structure or simplify the graphic
`stroke-dasharray` on `<circle>` / `<rect>` | Use `<path>` for dashed strokes (Gameface engine limit)
Both `mask` and `clip-path` with `url(#id)` | Avoid combining both on the same element; clip-path wins
Keyframes animating `width` without units | Add units (for example `100px`) in `@keyframes` for SVG CSS animation
Animating path `d` with arc commands | Review; elliptical arc animation may warn

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/svg/#where-rules-run]
## SVG in UI: Where rules run

- **HTML** — attributes and inline `style` on SVG elements, plus CSS in `<style>` blocks
- **JSX / TSX** — the same for component SVG trees
- **CSS files** — selectors that target SVG shapes and `@keyframes` used for SVG motion

Optional rule `gameface/html-svg-tspan-ignored` is off by default; enable it if you want a reminder that `<tspan>` styling is merged into the parent `<text>`.

For official support details, see [Gameface SVG Support](https://docs.coherent-labs.com/cpp-gameface/content_development/supported_features_tables/svgsupport/) in the Coherent documentation.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#no-gameface-messages-after-setup]
## Troubleshooting: No gameface/ messages after setup

- Confirm `eslint.config.js` spreads `...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"]`.
- Run ESLint from the project root: `npx eslint path/to/your-file.html`.
- Check the file extension is covered (`.html`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`).
- Ensure the file is not under `ignores` (for example `dist/**`).

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#vue-vue-files-not-linted-in-the-editor]
## Troubleshooting: Vue .vue files not linted in the editor

- Add `"vue"` to `eslint.validate` in `.vscode/settings.json` (see Installation).
- Ensure `eslint.config.js` spreads `...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"]`—the preset registers `vue-eslint-parser` for `**/*.vue`.
- `<style>` blocks are linted via `vue-sfc-css-*` rules on the same `.vue` file (not as separate virtual files).

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#svelte-svelte-files-not-linted-in-the-editor]
## Troubleshooting: Svelte .svelte files not linted in the editor

- Add `"svelte"` to `eslint.validate` in `.vscode/settings.json` (see Installation).
- Ensure `eslint.config.js` spreads `...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"]`—the preset registers `svelte-eslint-parser` for `**/*.svelte`.
- `<style>` blocks are linted via `svelte-sfc-css-*` rules on the same `.svelte` file (not as separate virtual files).

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#editor-shows-unknown-property-but-eslint-does-not]
## Troubleshooting: Editor shows “unknown property” but ESLint does not

VS Code and other editors often validate CSS separately from ESLint. `coh-*` properties for example may look invalid in the editor even when Gameface supports them. Use [VS Code custom CSS data](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/css#_css-specific-settings) or adjust editor CSS lint — not this plugin.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#scss-variables-skip-some-warnings]
## Troubleshooting: SCSS variables skip some warnings

Rules see `$variable` values as unresolved text, so some property/value checks are skipped on those lines. That is expected; keep critical Gameface constraints in plain CSS or literals where possible.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#too-many-html-partial-warnings]
## Troubleshooting: Too many HTML partial warnings

Relax or disable `gameface/html-partial-features`, or switch its mode in Configuration:

```js
"gameface/html-partial-features": ["warn", { mode: "tag-warn" }],
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#migrating-from-htmlhint--stylelint]
## Troubleshooting: Migrating from HTMLHint / Stylelint

The previous workflow was to use [HTMLLint](https://docs.coherent-labs.com/cpp-gameface/content_development/htmllint/) and [CSS Linter](https://docs.coherent-labs.com/cpp-gameface/content_development/csslinting/).

Now you can adopt this plugin gradually and stop using previous HTMLLint and CSS Linter. Enable `flat/recommended` for HTML and CSS first, then expand to JSX/TS, Vue, or Svelte in your project if needed. Once you adopted `eslint-plugin-gameface` you can safely remove `HTMLLint` and `CSS Linter`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/troubleshooting/#still-stuck]
## Troubleshooting: Still stuck?

Check the exact **rule id** in the ESLint message (for example `gameface/css-no-unsupported-properties`) and look it up in Rules reference to see what it enforces and how to turn it off.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/]
## Vue SFC

Vue **single-file components** (`.vue`) are linted by the recommended preset. The plugin parses the SFC with `vue-eslint-parser` and runs Gameface checks on each block.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/#what-is-checked-per-block]
## Vue SFC: What is checked per block

Block | Rules (prefix) | Notes
`<template>` | `vue-*`, `vue-inline-css-*`, `vue-databind-*`, `vue-svg-*` | Same coverage as HTML/JSX for markup, `:style`, `data-bind-*`, and inline SVG
`<script>` / `<script setup>` | `js-*` | Unsupported globals and partial API access (JS or TS via nested parser)
`<style>` / `<style lang="scss">` | `vue-sfc-css-*` | Same CSS checks as `.css` files and HTML `<style>` blocks

You do **not** need to install `vue-eslint-parser` or `eslint-plugin-vue` separately—they are dependencies of **eslint-plugin-gameface**. The preset registers them for `**/*.vue` files.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/#style--object-vs-string]
## Vue SFC: :style — object vs string

The linter handles both common Vue forms:

- **Object** — `:style="{ alignContent: 'space-between' }"` or `:style="{ 'align-content': 'space-between' }"`\
  Property names and partial **values** on keys are checked (`vue-inline-css-*`).
- **String** — `style="display: flex"` or `:style="'color: red'"`\
  Full CSS text is parsed, including unsupported **functions**, keyframes limits, and SVG keyframe rules.

Some restrictions (for example `var()` inside `@keyframes` in a style string) apply only to **string** styles, not object literals—same as JSX. See Rules reference — Vue `:style`.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/#data-bind--with-v-bind]
## Vue SFC: data-bind-* with v-bind

Gameface data binding works with plain and bound attributes:

```vue
<div data-bind-value="{{Model.score}}"></div>
<div :data-bind-value="'{{Model.score}}'"></div>
```

All six `vue-databind-*` rules mirror the HTML and JSX counterparts. See Data binding.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/#example-eslintconfigjs]
## Vue SFC: Example eslint.config.js

```js
import gameface from "eslint-plugin-gameface";

export default [
  { ignores: ["**/node_modules/**", "dist/**"] },
  ...gameface.configs["flat/recommended"],
  {
    settings: {
      gameface: {
        modelsDir: "Gameface-models",
      },
    },
  },
];
```

No extra `.vue` block is required—the preset includes parser, processor (for `eslint-disable` comment directives), and all `vue-*` / `vue-sfc-css-*` rules.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/vue/#vs-code]
## Vue SFC: VS Code

Add `"vue"` to `eslint.validate` so the ESLint extension lints `.vue` files while you edit. See Installation.

For every rule id and default severity, see Rules reference.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/]
## What gets checked

The recommended preset runs **Gameface-specific** rules on top of normal HTML and CSS parsing. Below is what you can expect in day-to-day work—not every possible rule, but the main categories.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#stylesheets-css-scss]
## What gets checked: Stylesheets (.css, .scss)

- CSS **properties** Gameface does not support
- **Partial** support (for example only some keyword values work)
- Unsupported **functions** such as `clamp()` or `min()` where Gameface reports them as missing
- **Selectors** and pseudos that are unsupported or only partially supported
- Documented limits: `var()` / `calc()` inside `@keyframes`, `var()` with a fallback argument, `calc()` mixing `%` with px and similar units
- SVG-related animation rules in CSS (units in keyframes, stroke dash on non-path elements, and similar)

SCSS files are parsed in a tolerant mode so Sass variables and nesting do not block the run; lines that still use unresolved `$variables` may skip some value checks. Rules nested under SCSS suffix selectors such as `&-option`, `&__item` and `&--active` are linted the same as any other nested rule.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#html-html]
## What gets checked: HTML (.html)

- Tags Gameface parses but does not implement (for example some form and table elements, depending on configuration)
- Partially supported elements when you use attributes Gameface does not handle
- **`data-bind-*`** spelling, `{{ }}` syntax, `bind-for`, class toggles, and model paths
- CSS inside `<style>` blocks and `style="..."` attributes—the same unsupported property/function/selector checks as in `.css` files
- SVG inside HTML: disallowed elements, mask/clip conflicts, stroke dash on wrong shapes

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#jsx-and-tsx-jsx-tsx]
## What gets checked: JSX and TSX (.jsx, .tsx)

- The same **data binding** checks as HTML on your components
- **Inline `style`** — both forms are linted, in different ways:
  - **`style={{ … }}`** — unsupported **property names** and partial **values** on object keys (for example `style={{ alignContent: 'stretch' }}`)
  - **`style="..."` / `style={'...'}`** — full CSS text, including unsupported **functions**, keyframes limits, and SVG keyframe rules
- **SVG** trees in components

See Rules reference — JSX `style` props for which rules apply to object vs string styles.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#vue-sfc-vue]
## What gets checked: Vue SFC (.vue)

- **`<template>`** — unsupported/partial tags (`vue-parsed-no-impl`, `vue-partial-features`), `data-bind-*` (`vue-databind-*`), `:style` / `style=""` (`vue-inline-css-*`), and SVG (`vue-svg-*`)
- **`<script>` / `<script setup>`** — `js-*` rules on the script block (JavaScript or TypeScript)
- **`<style>`** — `vue-sfc-css-*` rules (same coverage as `.css` and HTML embedded styles), including `lang="scss"` blocks

See Vue SFC for block-by-block detail.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#svelte-sfc-svelte]
## What gets checked: Svelte SFC (.svelte)

- **Markup** — unsupported/partial tags (`svelte-parsed-no-impl`, `svelte-partial-features`), `data-bind-*` (`svelte-databind-*`), `style` / `style={expr}` (`svelte-inline-css-*`), and SVG (`svelte-svg-*`)
- **`<script>` / `<script lang="ts">`** — `js-*` rules on the script block (JavaScript or TypeScript)
- **`<style>`** — `svelte-sfc-css-*` rules (same coverage as `.css` and HTML embedded styles), including `lang="scss"` blocks

See Svelte SFC for block-by-block detail.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#javascript-and-typescript-js-jsx-ts-tsx]
## What gets checked: JavaScript and TypeScript (.js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx)

- References to **globals** Gameface does not provide (for example some browser APIs)
- **Partial** APIs where only some members exist (reported as warnings by default)

Checks are static: dynamic property access and patterns ESLint cannot see without type information may not be reported.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/eslint-plugin-gameface/guides/what-gets-checked/#what-is-not-checked-today]
## What gets checked: What is not checked (today)

- Standalone `.svg` asset files (only SVG inside HTML/JSX/Vue/Svelte templates)
- Every browser CSS feature—only what Gameface documents as unsupported or partial
- Runtime binding errors—only syntax and known unsupported features

For every rule id, default severity, and how to change them, see Rules reference.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/changelog/#110]
## Changelog: 1.1.0 Latest

Feature `track` records components that are already in a project but were never registered under `gameface-ui-components`, so `status` and `update` can see them. It compares every file against the registry: components that match are recorded at their real version, components whose files differ are recorded as `0.0.0` so `update` picks them up, and components that are not present are left alone. Only `package.json` is written - component files are never touched unless you pick the update option.

Feature `--hard` reinstalls components even when their recorded version already matches the registry. Use it to restore a component you have edited, or to refresh the shared files a component depends on.

Feature `--verbose` lists the individual files behind each result instead of just the counts.

Improvement The **Setup required** note now names the steps a project is actually missing and links the guide. It is based on the project itself rather than on whether the CLI has run before, so a Gameface UI project no longer sees it and a project that still needs setting up keeps being told.

Improvement `add` and `update` now write only the files that differ from the published version, instead of rewriting every file of every component they touch. Updating a project that is behind by a few files no longer produces a diff spanning its whole component tree.

Fix Binary files are no longer corrupted on install. Component files were decoded as UTF-8 text before being written, which damaged assets such as the icon fallback image and any font shipped with a component.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/changelog/#100]
## Changelog: 1.0.0

Feature Initial release of `gameface-cli`.

Feature `add <components...>` installs one or more components together with their transitive dependencies. Shared dependencies are downloaded once and `npm install` runs a single time, however many components are requested.

Feature `update [components...]` brings installed components to the current published version. With no arguments it sweeps everything tracked in `package.json`, leaving up-to-date components untouched.

Feature `status` lists installed components with their versions, flags the ones that have updates available, and reports how many more components the library offers.

Feature Installed components and their versions are recorded under `gameface-ui-components` in the project’s `package.json`, preserving its existing indentation.

Feature `--yes` skips every confirmation prompt for non-interactive and CI use, and `--help` prints usage.

Feature Setup instructions are printed the first time components are installed into a project that has not used the CLI before.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/]
## Overview

`gameface-cli` adds and updates **individual Gameface UI components** inside an existing project. Instead of pulling the whole library, you install the components you actually use, and the CLI keeps them current as new versions ship.

It is not a scaffolder. If you are starting from nothing, use `create-gameface-app` with the **Gameface UI** template to create the project first. `gameface-cli` only ever operates on a project that already exists.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#requirements]
## Overview: Requirements

A [Gameface UI](https://gameface-ui.coherent-labs.com/) or a SolidJS project set up. The CLI checks for `solid-js` in your `package.json` and stops if it isn’t there.

Only the [Gameface UI](https://gameface-ui.coherent-labs.com/) project is ready to use straight away. The `solid-js` template that can be downloaded from the create-gameface-app CLI does not have the aliases and style variables that components rely on. If you are using that one, or on a Solid project of your own, follow the one-time setup in Existing projects.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#quick-start]
## Overview: Quick start

**npm:**

```
npx gameface-cli add Dropdown
```

**pnpm:**

```
pnpm dlx gameface-cli add Dropdown
```

**yarn:**

```
yarn dlx gameface-cli add Dropdown
```

That copies `Dropdown` into `src/components/`, along with everything it depends on, and records what it installed in your `package.json`.

**Editing installed components:** Installed components are managed by the CLI, so `update` replaces them with the newer version. Any local changes you have made to them will be replaced along with the file.

If you need different behaviour, the safer options are to use the component’s props, or to wrap it in your own component under `src/custom-components/`, which the CLI never touches. If something is missing or broken, an issue or a pull request against the library is worth more than a local patch.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#commands]
## Overview: Commands (1/3)

#### add

Installs one or more components, together with their dependencies.

```bash
npx gameface-cli add Dropdown
npx gameface-cli add Dropdown Scroll TextSlider
```

Adding several at once is cheaper than adding them one at a time, since shared dependencies are downloaded once and if external dependencies are missing `npm install` runs a single time at the end.

This is also how you pick up components released since you created your project. `update` only refreshes what you already have, it never adds anything new.

**Dependency upgrades:** If a component you are installing shares a dependency with something you already have, that dependency is brought up to the current version too.

For example, if you already have `Dropdown` and it has pulled the `Utility/Navigation` at v1.0.0 alongside it, and you add `TextSlider` which also depends on the `Navigation` component, the CLI will upgrade `Utility/Navigation` to its latest version for you.

#### update

Brings installed components up to the latest published version.

```bash
npx gameface-cli update              # everything you have installed
npx gameface-cli update Dropdown     # just this one
```

With no arguments it sweeps everything tracked in your `package.json`, updates whatever is out of date, and leaves current components alone.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#commands]
## Overview: Commands (2/3)

The command updates files related just to Gameface UI components in your project. Your own code, your views, and your config files (`tsconfig.json`, `vite.config`, `package.json` scripts) are never touched. Library changes that need a config edit are called out in the changelog and applied by hand.

Only files whose contents differ from the published version are written. A component that is out of date by a single file produces a single-file diff rather than a rewrite of the whole component and everything it depends on, so what you review afterwards is what actually changed.

#### track

Registers Gameface UI components that are already in your project but were never recorded under `gameface-ui-components`. Without this, `status` and `update` cannot see them.

```bash
npx gameface-cli track
```

It compares every file in your project against the registry and sorts each component into one of three outcomes:

Result | What it means | What gets recorded
Up to date | Every file matches the published version | its real version
Behind | One or more files are missing or different | `0.0.0`, so `update` picks it up
Not installed | None of its files are present | nothing

Anything recorded as `0.0.0` counts as out of date, so the next `update` restores it to the published version.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#commands]
## Overview: Commands (3/3)

**`track` never writes component files.** It only adds entries to `package.json`, and it never modifies or removes entries that are already there - so it is safe to re-run, and doubles as a repair after a bad merge drops keys from your `package.json`. When it finishes you can either record the versions and stop, or record and run the update immediately.

**When you need it:** Projects scaffolded by a recent `create-gameface-app` already have their components recorded. You need `track` if your project predates the CLI (Gameface UI v3.1.0 or earlier), if you copied components in by hand, or if the version recording failed while scaffolding.

#### status

Shows what you have installed and what has moved on without you.

```bash
npx gameface-cli status
```

```plaintext
┌  gameface-cli
│
◇  Gameface UI v3.2.0
│
├  Installed Components ────────────╮
│                                   │
│  Dropdown    v1.0.0 → v1.1.0      │
│  TextSlider  v1.1.0 (up to date)  │
│                                   │
├───────────────────────────────────╯
│
●  12 more components available in the library.
│
└  1 out of 2 outdated · run `gameface-cli update` to upgrade
```

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#options]
## Overview: Options

Flag | Alias | Description
`--yes` | `-y` | Answer every confirmation prompt with yes.
`--help` | `-h` | Print usage information and exit.

Two more flags apply to specific commands only: `--verbose` on `add`, `update` and `track`, and `--hard` on `update`.

#### --verbose

Lists the individual files behind each result instead of just the counts.

On `add` and `update` it prints every file written rather than the directories they live in. On `track` it names the files that are missing or differ under each component, and reports the components it skipped as not installed.

```bash
npx gameface-cli track --verbose
npx gameface-cli update --verbose
```

#### --hard

Reinstalls components even when their recorded version already matches the registry, which `update` would normally skip.

```bash
npx gameface-cli update Dropdown --hard   # restore a component you edited
npx gameface-cli update --hard            # refresh everything, shared files included
```

Use it to restore a stock component after editing it in place, or to refresh the shared files that components depend on. Those shared files carry no version of their own, so nothing else can tell that they have drifted.

**Caution:**

`--hard` overwrites local edits without asking, and with no arguments it reinstalls everything you have. Commit your work first.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/#what-it-changes-in-your-project]
## Overview: What it changes in your project

Two things, and nothing else.

**Component files** are written under `src/`, at the same paths they have in the library.

**A record of what you installed** is added to your `package.json`, under `gameface-ui-components`:

```json
"gameface-ui-components": {
  "Dropdown": "1.0.0",
  "TextSlider": "1.1.0"
}
```

`status` and `update` compare these versions against the ones the library publishes. Anything that differs is out of date.

**Don't edit the gameface-ui-components property by hand:** This entry is the CLI’s only record of what you have installed, and it is trusted as-is. Editing it by hand makes every command report the wrong thing: lower a version and `update` will reinstall a component you already have, raise one and it will skip a component that is genuinely out of date, remove an entry and the component stops being tracked at all.

Commit it with the rest of your `package.json` and let the CLI maintain it.

Nothing else in your project is modified, and the rest of your `package.json` keeps its existing formatting.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/]
## Existing projects

Projects created with the **`gameface-ui` template** from `create-gameface-app` are already wired up and need nothing from this page.

**Components already in your project?:** If your project was created from the Gameface UI template before this CLI existed, its components are on disk but not recorded, so `status` and `update` cannot see them. Run `npx gameface-cli track` once to register them. It only writes to the `package.json` - your component files are left alone. See `track`.

Every other starting point needs a one-time setup, including the plain `solid` template. `create-gameface-app` scaffolds several frameworks, and only the [Gameface UI](https://gameface-ui.coherent-labs.com/) template ships the aliases and style variables that components depend on.

The CLI prints a **Setup required** note the first time it installs into a project it doesn’t recognise. This page is what that note refers to.

**Note:** The CLI does not wire this up for you on purpose. `tsconfig.json` allows comments and `vite.config` is executable code, so neither can be edited automatically without risking your existing configuration.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#setup]
## Existing projects: Setup (1/2)

1. **Install `sass`**

   Component stylesheets are written in SCSS. It is a build-time tool rather than a runtime dependency, so the CLI does not install it for you.

   **npm:**

   ```
   npm install -D sass
   ```

   **pnpm:**

   ```
   pnpm add -D sass
   ```

   **yarn:**

   ```
   yarn add -D sass
   ```

2. **Add the `@components` alias to `tsconfig.json`**

   Components import each other through this alias, so TypeScript needs to resolve it:

   ```json
   {
     "compilerOptions": {
       "baseUrl": ".",
       "paths": {
         "@components/*": ["src/components/*"],
         "@assets/*": ["src/assets/*"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Add the same aliases to your Vite config**

   TypeScript path mappings only affect type checking. Vite resolves imports at build time and needs to be told separately:

   ```ts
   import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
   import solid from 'vite-plugin-solid';
   import path from 'node:path';

   export default defineConfig({
     plugins: [solid()],
     resolve: {
       alias: {
         '@components': path.resolve(__dirname, './src/components'),
         '@assets': path.resolve(__dirname, './src/assets'),
       },
     },
   });
   ```

4. **Set up the style variables**

   Every component stylesheet expects a set of shared SCSS variables to be available. Create the file at `src/assets/scss/_variables.scss`:

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#setup]
## Existing projects: Setup (2/2)

   ```scss
   // Your design tokens: colours, spacing, typography.
   // Component styles reference these, so the names must exist.
    $primaryColor: #868599;
    $secondaryColor: #3e3d5d;
    $disabledColor: #bdbdbd;
    $textColor: #ffffff;
    $disabledTextColor: #dddedf;
   ```

   Then inject it into every SCSS file so components don’t have to import it themselves:

   ```ts
   export default defineConfig({
     // ...plugins and resolve as above
     css: {
       preprocessorOptions: {
         scss: {
           additionalData: `@use '@assets/scss/variables' as *;`,
         },
       },
     },
   });
   ```

Once that is in place, `npx gameface-cli add <component>` behaves exactly as it does in a Gameface UI project.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#what-a-set-up-project-looks-like]
## Existing projects: What a set-up project looks like

A plain Solid project after the setup above, with one component installed. **Highlighted** files are the ones you write or edit yourself.

- package.json the CLI records what it installed here, under `gameface-ui-components`
- **tsconfig.json** the `@components` and `@assets` paths from step 2
- **vite.config.ts** the matching aliases and the SCSS injection from steps 3 and 4
- **Directorysrc**
  - main.tsx
  - App.tsx
  - **Directoryassets**
    - **Directoryscss**
      - **\_variables.scss** your design tokens, injected into every stylesheet
  - **Directorycomponents your components and the CLI’s, side by side**
    - **DirectoryBaseComponent**
      - BaseComponent.tsx
    - **DirectoryBasic**
      - **DirectoryButton**
        - Button.tsx
        - Button.module.scss
    - **DirectoryUtility**
      - **DirectoryNavigation**
        - Navigation.tsx
        - …
    - **Directorytypes**
      - ComponentProps.d.ts
      - …
    - **Directoryutils**
      - waitForFrames.ts
      - …
    - **DirectoryHUD yours, and the CLI will never touch it**
      - HUD.tsx
      - HUD.module.scss

Only `Button` was asked for. `BaseComponent`, `Utility/Navigation`, `types` and `utils` came along as its dependencies, which is why the folder looks fuller than a single install suggests. Those shared folders are reused by every component, so the next few installs add much less.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#living-alongside-your-own-components]
## Existing projects: Living alongside your own components

There is no separate folder to keep your components in. Put them wherever you like, `src/components/` included - the CLI has no opinion about what else is in there.

What it does have is a fixed list of paths it owns. On every `add` and `update` it writes those paths from the registry, overwriting whatever is there without merging and without asking. Inside `src/components/`, that list is:

```plaintext
BaseComponent/  Basic/  Complex/  Feedback/  Layout/  Media/  Utility/  types/  utils/
```

**Path collisions:** The one rule is not to put your own files at a path the CLI already claims. `src/components/Basic/Button/Button.tsx` belongs to Gameface UI, and a `Button` of your own written there disappears the first time anyone installs or updates the Gameface UI one. Naming your component `Button` is fine. Path like `src/components/HUD/Button.tsx` is safe if adding the `Button` component. It is only the collision of the full path that costs you the file.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#components-that-need-a-full-gameface-project]
## Existing projects: Components that need a full Gameface project

[`Icon`](https://gameface-ui.coherent-labs.com/components/media/icon/) and [`Keybinds`](https://gameface-ui.coherent-labs.com/components/basic/keybinds/) are not available outside a Gameface UI project. They depend on generated type files, an icon-generation script, and gamepad glyph assets that only exist in the full template, so installing them here would leave you with components that don’t build.

If you need them, start from `create-gameface-app` with the `gameface-ui` template instead.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#troubleshooting]
## Existing projects: Troubleshooting (1/2)

Problem | Fix
`Cannot find module '@components/...'` | The alias is missing from `tsconfig.json`, from your Vite config, or from both. Each needs its own copy: TypeScript uses it for type checking, Vite for resolving the actual import.
`Undefined variable` errors from SCSS | Either `_variables.scss` does not exist, `additionalData` is not injecting it, or the variable names do not match. Component styles reference specific names such as `$primaryColor`, `$secondaryColor` and `$textColor`, so your own tokens have to use those names rather than equivalents of your own choosing.
`npm installation failed` | The component files were written, but installing their npm dependencies did not work. The CLI prints the exact command to run by hand. A pre-existing unresolvable dependency in your `package.json` is the usual cause, since npm resolves the whole tree on any install.
`Gameface UI components require a SolidJS project` | `solid-js` is not in your `package.json`. Install it, or start from the `gameface-ui` template.
`status` shows almost nothing installed, but the components are clearly there | They were never recorded under `gameface-ui-components`. Run `npx gameface-cli track` to register what is already on disk.
`track` reports a component as behind that you never touched | Its files differ from the published version, which usually means they are simply from an older release. Run with `--verbose` to see exactly which files differ.

---
[SOURCE: https://frontend-tools.coherent-labs.com/gameface-cli/getting-started/existing-projects/#troubleshooting]
## Existing projects: Troubleshooting (2/2)

Problem | Fix
Styles are missing after an update | The update replaced a stock component you had edited in place. Re-apply the change as a wrapper or through props so it lives at a path of your own, then re-run the update.
A file of your own disappeared after `add` or `update` | It was at a path the registry owns. Recover it from source control and move it out of `BaseComponent/`, `Basic/`, `Complex/`, `Feedback/`, `Layout/`, `Media/`, `Utility/`, `types/` and `utils/` - anywhere else under `src/components/` is safe.
